location.evidence_quote: Satellite image of a Yanomami village in the Brazilian Amazon.
location.notes: Location details are group-specific; Yanomami/Venezuela from 'Venezuelan Amazon', Matses from 'Peruvian Amazon', Tunapuco from 'Andean highlands' (Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity).

subject_id.notes: Individual subject identifiers are only referenced as being summarized in Supplementary Table 1, not provided in the main text.

sample_id.notes: No individual sample IDs given in the provided text; details said to be in Supplementary Table 1.

subcohort.notes: Group-level comparisons are captured under 'subgroups' (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US); no further subcohort splitting reported.

control.notes: Study is an observational comparative metagenomic study; no explicit case/control framework reported.

country.evidence_quote: the Matses from the Peruvian Amazon ( n = 24)
country.notes: Brazil, Venezuela, and United States explicitly named per group; Tunapuco only described as 'Andean highlands' without an explicit country name in the text.

body_site.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample
body_site.section: Materials and Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
body_site.notes: Explicitly stated for Yanomami/Brazil; other reanalyzed groups (Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US) are described as gut microbiome datasets, implying fecal samples but not re-described in this text (inferred for these).

days_from_first_collection.notes: Study appears cross-sectional (single stool sample per subject); no longitudinal time points reported.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: The Yanomami is the largest semi-nomadic hunter–gatherer group of the Americas
lifestyle.notes: Tunapuco described as 'a rural agricultural community' (Bioinformatics Processing); US described as 'urban-industrialized' but not assigned a lifestyle term matching the enum options.

westernized.notes: Traditional groups (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco) contrasted throughout with the 'urban-industrialized' US group.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208
ncbi_accession.notes: Accession only given for the newly generated Yanomami/Brazil data; other groups' data cited from prior publications without accession numbers stated here.

age.notes: Ages said to be summarized in Supplementary Table 1, not reported in main text.

sex.evidence_quote: gender information of the individuals were also acquired
sex.section: Materials and Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
sex.notes: Sex/gender data acquired but individual or subgroup counts not reported in main text; only used for a PERMANOVA test with no reported male/female counts.

dietary_restriction.notes: General diet described qualitatively (e.g., 'low in fat and salt, and high in fruits, fiber, and sylvatic animals') but no formal dietary restriction category reported.

disease.evidence_quote: Common chronic diseases in modern societies, as atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami
disease.notes: Statement is general to the Yanomami ethnic group (not separated by Brazil/Venezuela); no direct disease diagnosis data reported for any subject.

disease_details.evidence_quote: Common chronic diseases in modern societies, as atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami
disease_details.notes: No explicit disease label given; participants are traditional hunter-gatherers described as free of common modern chronic diseases, inferred as healthy status.

biomarker_name.notes: Paper reports taxonomic 'biomarkers' (bacterial genera) via LDA/LEfSe but these are not clinical biomarkers with defined value/unit pairs suitable for this field.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable to this gut microbiome study; no tumor-related data reported.

uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Included as supplementary metadata not covered by other schema fields.

study_name.notes: No canonical study name (e.g., 'AuthorYear') given in text; only title and BioProject accession are provided.

curator.notes: Curator name not part of paper content; this refers to metadata curator, not authors.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the provided paper text; paper_id may correspond to PMID but this was not confirmed within the text itself.

target_condition.notes: Study focuses on healthy traditional and urban populations' gut microbiome diversity, not a specific disease/phenotype target condition.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: No mention of antibiotic exclusion criteria in the Methods.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Total DNA was extracted from 15 stool samples with FastDNA ® SPIN Kit (MP Biomedicals), following the manufacturer’s instructions.
dna_extraction_kit.section: Materials and Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Surface form retained; closest allowed value category is 'MP Biomedicals'.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq ® 2500 sequencer (Oswaldo Cruz Foundation, high-throughput sequencing platform)
sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
sequencing_platform.notes: Corresponds to allowed value 'Illumina HiSeq'; surface form retained as per instructions.

host_species.evidence_quote: Non-host reads (∼198 million reads) were used in further analysis... mapped to a human reference genome (Hg38) using Bowtie2
host_species.notes: Host species is implied by human reference genome mapping and human stool sample collection from Yanomami participants.
